cards.title: Everything that happened, in order
cards.text: 25 on-track passes, 6 pit stops, 1 car that never finished.

cards.title: 12 places changed hands on track before the first lap was done
cards.text: 22 cars into the first corner on cold tyres and full tanks.
bullets: Perez gained the most by the end of it, 3 places
cards.note: Most of this is the pack sorting itself out. Some of it decides the sprint.

cards.title: Lawson starts P18. Where does he finish?
cards.text: 23 laps to make up ground from there.

cards.title: Who has the fastest lap on the board at the flag?
cards.text: It usually lands late, when the car is light and the track has rubber all over it.
cards.reveal: Antonelli on lap 11, 1:14.380, in a Mercedes.

cards.title: Albon: 4 passes
cards.text: More than anybody else out there, in a Williams.
bullets: P22 on the grid, P19 at the flag
cards.note: Only moves made on track count, with the car ahead at racing speed.

cards.title: 17 lap times deleted
cards.text: The white line is the track, and the lap simply stops counting if you leave it.
bullets: Antonelli, Bortoleto, Hulkenberg and 1 other lost 2 each, the most of anybody
cards.note: Keep doing it and it turns into a penalty.

cards.title: Lawson and Antonelli hit 353 km/h
cards.text: The fastest car in a straight line is often not the fastest car over a lap.
bullets: Top speed says as much about wing level, and about sitting in somebody's tow, as it does about the engine

cards.title: Antonelli: 1:14.380
cards.text: The quickest anybody went all sprint, in a Mercedes.
bullets: Set on lap 11 of 23, early for a fastest lap, with plenty of fuel still on board
A sprint has never paid a point for it

cards.title: One of these three does not see the chequered flag. Who?
cards.text: Nothing on the timing screens says it is coming.
cards.reveal: Alonso, on lap 16 of 23. The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: 5 incidents looked at
cards.text: Every one of them logged by race control during the sprint.
bullets: Lap 12: Hulkenberg, leaving the track and gaining an advantage
2 ended in a penalty, 2 in no further action and 1 left for after the sprint

cards.kicker: Your call on the pit wall
cards.title: You are Norris, 0.5s behind Russell and going nowhere. Now what?
cards.text: Stuck behind another car your tyres overheat and the car will not turn. Stopping first gives you clean track for two or three laps, which is the whole trick behind the undercut.

choices.label: Box now and undercut
choices.sub: Fresh tyres, clean air, two laps to make it pay

choices.label: Stay out and overcut
choices.sub: Let him stop first, then push on an empty track

choices.label: Forget strategy, pass him
choices.sub: Send it and take the risk

outcomes.box: You spend about 24s in the lane and come out in traffic, betting that two fast laps on new tyres are worth more than the place you just gave up.
outcomes.wait: You stay on old rubber while he gets new ones, and you need clean air plus a mistake from him to make it work.
outcomes.attack: Passing a car with the same tyres on the same fuel is the hardest thing in the sport, and running into the back of him ends both races.

cards.reveal: Norris did not stop. He finished P2, Russell P1.

cards.title: Alonso is out
cards.text: His sprint ends on lap 16 of 23, in an Aston Martin.
bullets: P18 at the start of lap 15
Started P15
cards.note: The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: Russell had the quickest median racing lap
cards.text: No lap 1, no laps in or out of the pits, nothing behind the safety car or the VSC, and the slow outliers trimmed. It does not always match the result.

cards.title: Yellow flags out 1 time
cards.text: Race control waves a yellow for anything on or near the track that should not be there.
bullets: A yellow means slow down and do not overtake in that part of the track

cards.title: Hadjar went the other way: 13 places lost
cards.text: Qualifying promised one thing and the sprint delivered another.
bullets: P8 on the grid, P21 at the flag
2 stops when most of the field made none
Qualifying rewards whoever can put one lap together. A sprint asks for 23 of them

cards.title: Perez: 10 laps within a second of the car ahead
cards.text: The longest unbroken run like it in the sprint, from lap 9 to lap 18, at racing speed.
bullets: 7 other drivers had a run of five laps or more like it
cards.note: Following closely costs the car downforce and cooks the front tyres, so sitting there is harder than it looks.

cards.title: Lawson: P18 on the grid, P11 at the flag
cards.text: 7 places gained.
bullets: 3 on-track passes along the way
1 car that started ahead of him retired

cards.title: 2 penalties handed out
cards.text: Given by the stewards during the sprint.
bullets: Hulkenberg: a 10s penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage
Perez: a 10s penalty for forcing another driver off the track
cards.note: A time penalty is served at the next stop, or added to the final time when there is no stop left.

cards.title: Lap 21: an incident between Perez and Lawson at Turn 13. What do you give?
cards.text: Race control has flagged it and it lands on your desk. Same call the stewards had to make.
state: Forcing Another Driver Off The Track at Turn 13

outcomes.none: You let it go. Nobody loses a place at a desk, and the driver behind spends the rest of the race on the radio.
outcomes.5: Five seconds gets added at the next stop, or to the final time if there is no stop left. Usually one position, sometimes none.
outcomes.10: Ten seconds is a real punishment and it almost always costs track position, which is why teams argue so hard about it.

cards.reveal: The stewards gave Perez a 10s penalty. He still finished P14.

cards.title: 17 of 22 cars never stopped
cards.text: One set of tyres took most of the field to the flag.
bullets: On one set the whole way: Mediums for 13, softs for 3, hards for Lindblad
cards.note: Every lap you stretch is a lap you do not lose in the pit lane.

cards.title: Russell wins it
cards.text: P1 Russell · P2 Norris · P3 Antonelli.
bullets: After 23 laps, Norris crossed the line 1.272s behind
cards.note: Less than the time it takes to read this sentence.

cards.title: How far behind was Norris at the flag?
cards.text: 23 laps, about 29 minutes of racing, and it comes down to this one number.
cards.reveal: 1.272 seconds after 23 laps. A trip down the pit lane took about 24s today, which is 19 times the margin this sprint was decided by.
